name: ticket-manager
description: A compact issue and board sidebar for VS Code with Jira MCP, demo, and file-backed modes.

scripts.build:install: npm run build && npm run install:all

viewsWelcome.contents:

Configure a project to get started.
[$(plug) Connections & Boards](command:ticketManager.openConnectionsManager)

ticketManager.backendMode.description: Choose whether the app uses Jira MCP, Demo, GitHub, GitLab, Live Folder, or User Workspace mode.

ticketManager.connectionType.description: Legacy Jira MCP transport selector retained for compatibility with existing setup flows and integration tests.

ticketManager.stdioCommand.description: Legacy Jira MCP stdio command retained for compatibility with existing setup flows and integration tests.

ticketManager.stdioArgs.description: Legacy Jira MCP stdio command arguments retained for compatibility with existing setup flows and integration tests.

ticketManager.stdioCwd.description: Legacy Jira MCP stdio working directory retained for compatibility with existing setup flows and integration tests.

ticketManager.httpUrl.description: Legacy Jira MCP HTTP endpoint URL retained for compatibility with existing setup flows and integration tests.

ticketManager.connections.description: Named backend connections. Each entry is one configured backend instance (Jira server, GitLab host, Live Folder root, etc.). Use the Ticket Manager: Connections command to manage these via the UI.

id.description: Stable identifier for this connection. Used to reference it from tracked boards and secrets.

settings.description: Mode-specific settings (URL, project key, MCP command, folder path, etc.). Secrets are stored separately in VS Code SecretStorage.

ticketManager.boards.description: Boards the user has explicitly chosen to track. Each entry references a connection by id and a board id native to that backend.

connectionId.description: Id of the connection this board belongs to (must match an entry in ticketManager.connections).

displayName.description: Optional override for the board's display name in the sidebar.

ticketManager.jiraMcpSiteUrl.description: Base URL of the Jira instance that MCP tools connect to in Jira MCP mode. Used for display and as a fallback when no MCP connection reports a URL.

ticketManager.jiraMcpDefaultProjectKey.description: Default Jira project key for new issues created through the Jira MCP backend when the form does not specify one.

ticketManager.jiraMcpEpicKey.description: Optional Jira Epic key associated with this workspace in Jira MCP mode. Boards follow this epic and Jira issue creation uses it as the default parent epic.

ticketManager.jiraMcpEpicBoardName.description: Optional display name for the Jira MCP epic board in this workspace.

ticketManager.jiraMcpBoardJql.description: Optional Jira JQL query associated with this workspace in Jira MCP mode. When set, a JQL board is shown in addition to any linked epic board.

ticketManager.jiraMcpBoardName.description: Optional display name for the Jira MCP JQL board in this workspace.

ticketManager.enableCreateIdea.markdownDescription: Enable the **Create Idea** command and button (preview). When disabled, the command and its icon are hidden.

ticketManager.enableNewProject.markdownDescription: Enable the **New Project** wizard (preview). When disabled, the command is hidden from the Command Palette.

ticketManager.boardsSidebarPreviewMode.markdownDescription: Select the **Boards** sidebar layout. **Classic** uses separate views (Boards, EPICs, My Issues, Sessions, Issue Details). **Work Mode** uses a board-centric layout with boards as cards and nested agent sessions.

ticketManager.requestTimeoutMs.description: Timeout, in milliseconds, for MCP requests.

ticketManager.defaultPageSize.description: Number of issues to request per page.

ticketManager.delivery.defaultBaseBranch.markdownDescription: Default base branch to use when a Jira ticket does not specify one (e.g. `main`, `develop`). When empty, the agent will post a clarification comment asking for the branch.

ticketManager.delivery.autoMergeSubTasks.markdownDescription: When enabled (default), completed sub-task branches are automatically merged into the feature branch without creating a merge request. A single MR is raised from the feature branch to the base branch after all sub-tasks complete. When disabled, each sub-task creates its own MR targeting the feature branch.

ticketManager.workspaceMcpServerName.description: Optional workspace MCP server name to use from .vscode/mcp.json when Jira via MCP mode is not manually configured.

ticketManager.userMcpServerRef.description: Optional user/profile MCP server reference to use when Jira via MCP mode is not manually configured and no workspace MCP server is selected.

ticketManager.priorityColors.description: Colors for the priority indicator bar on ticket cards. Values can be hex colors or CSS linear gradients.

ticketManager.jiraBoardListIconColor.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon to the left of each board name in the Boards list when a **Jira** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#3b82f6`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.demoBoardListIconColor.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon beside board names when **Demo** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#a855f7`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.fileBoardListIconColor.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon beside board names when **File** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#22c55e`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.liveFolderPath.markdownDescription: Absolute path to a `plans` folder, `features` folder, or parent folder to search for `features/feature-NN-*/feature.md` and `story-*.md` files. Used when **Live Folder** mode is active.

ticketManager.liveFolderProjectKey.markdownDescription: Project key for issues derived from the live folder (e.g. `TRAKA`). Used when **Live Folder** mode is active.

ticketManager.liveFolderProjectName.markdownDescription: Human-readable project name for the live folder (e.g. `TrakaHIS Integration`). Used when **Live Folder** mode is active.

ticketManager.liveFolderAllowIssueCreati.markdownDescription: Allow Ticket Manager to create new markdown issue files when **Live Folder** mode is active. Disable this to keep the live folder read-only from the extension.

ticketManager.liveFolderBoardListIconCol.markdownDescription: Accent color for the small backend icon beside board names when **Live Folder** mode is active. Use hex (e.g. `#f59e0b`). Leave empty for the built-in default.

ticketManager.ai.provider.description: The single active AI provider Ticket Manager uses. Only Vercel AI Gateway is supported.

ticketManager.ai.credential.description: Deprecated for Vercel Gateway (API key is stored in Secret Storage). Kept for migration of older installs.

ticketManager.ai.agentName.description: Display and @mention name for the active AI provider. Leave empty to use the provider default label.

ticketManager.ai.runtimePath.description: Optional runtime override path for CLI-based providers.

ticketManager.ai.vercelUrl.description: Base URL for the Vercel AI Gateway when the active provider is vercel-gateway.

ticketManager.ai.defaultModel.description: Default AI model to store on newly created live-folder markdown tickets when a model is configured. Leave empty to omit the model field.

ticketManager.ai.analysisEnabled.description: Enable the per-issue analysis gate before assigning a ticket to AI.

ticketManager.ai.analysisDefaultPrompt.default:
You are a senior software engineer analysing a development ticket and any code/context provided.

Goal:
Explain the problem, determine a safe solution, and show the code-level changes required.
If acceptance criteria are missing, propose clear, testable acceptance criteria.

Inputs I may provide:
- Ticket title, description, acceptance criteria (if any)
- Code snippets, file paths, project/repo names, or architecture notes
- Errors/logs/examples of incorrect behaviour

Strict formatting rules:
- DO NOT use tables.
- DO NOT use HTML or HTML entities.
- Use plain text with headings and bullet points only.
- Use "-" for bullets.
- Code must appear only inside fenced code blocks.

Evidence and inference rules (IMPORTANT):
- Do not guess specific file paths, repos, libraries, or NuGet packages unless explicitly evidenced.
- If you infer something, label it "Inferred".
- If a referenced class/method/config is missing from the provided context, do NOT claim where it is.
  Instead: list possible sources (another repo, shared library, NuGet, generated code, legacy branch) and state what evidence would confirm it.

Blocker handling rules:
- Lack of full repo access is NOT automatically a blocker.
- Only call something a blocker if it prevents a safe change.
- When reporting a blocker, state:
  - What exactly is missing (symbol/contract/config/entry point/dependency)
  - Possible source type (repo/project/shared lib/NuGet/generated/etc.)
  - Why it blocks a safe fix
  - Minimal info needed to unblock (file path, project name, package reference, commit hash, sample payload)

Solution rules:
- Prefer safe, minimal, backwards-compatible fixes.
- If the change is small and the correct location is unclear, propose a local helper/utility approach as an option (and explain tradeoffs).
- Provide at most 2 solution options. Pick one recommended option with rationale.

Acceptance Criteria rules (MANDATORY):
- If acceptance criteria are present: assess if they are clear and testable; if not, propose improved ones.
- If acceptance criteria are missing: create "Proposed Acceptance Criteria" that are:
  - Testable and unambiguous
  - Directly derived from the ticket + provided evidence
  - Written as bullet points or Given/When/Then
  - Include at least one negative/edge-case criterion when relevant
- If a criterion relies on an assumption, label it "(Assumption)".
- Do not invent new scope; keep criteria aligned to the stated problem.

Output format (mandatory, keep concise):

1) Problem identified
- What is broken/incorrect
- Root cause (Confirmed vs Inferred)

2) Understanding of expected behaviour
- What should happen instead
- Constraints/assumptions (only if explicit or clearly implied)

3) Solution (high level)
- Recommended approach
- Option B (only if relevant)
- Key tradeoffs/safety notes

4) Code-level results (implementation-ready)
- Change list (by component or layer; do not invent file paths)
- Minimal patch snippets (diff or before/after)
- If location is unknown, show a safe helper/utility snippet and describe where it should be wired in (by symbol/interface/usage pattern, not file path)

5) Acceptance criteria
- Existing acceptance criteria: Present / Missing
- If present: issues (if any) and improved version (if needed)
- If missing: Proposed acceptance criteria (testable bullets)

6) Readiness, Confidence, Risk
- Readiness: Ready / Implementable with clarifications / Not ready
- Confidence: High / Medium / Low (based on evidence available)
- Risk: Low / Medium / High (impact + uncertainty)
- 2-5 bullets explaining why

7) Verification
- Tests/scenarios to prove the fix
- Any important edge cases

Now analyse the ticket and code below and produce the output in this exact format.
ticketManager.ai.analysisDefaultPrompt.description: Required default prompt used in the Analysis Window. If empty, analysis gating is treated as disabled at runtime.

ticketManager.ai.analysisDefaultModel.description: Default model used by the Analysis Window. Leave empty to fall back to ticketManager.ai.defaultModel.

ticketManager.ai.verboseActivityFeed.description: Show all event types (tool calls, permission requests, etc.) in the AI session activity feed. When disabled, only high-value events like messages, plans, and errors are shown.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryWorkflowEnabled.description: When enabled, Jira polling moves implementation-ready issues into the delivery workflow instead of posting the full AI conversation back into Jira comments.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryPublishCommand.description: Repository-specific command the AI delivery workflow must run inside the dedicated worktree to publish the MSI artifact.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryArtifactPattern.description: Glob or relative path pattern, from the delivery worktree root, that identifies the MSI artifact(s) to attach back to Jira.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryAgentWorkflowPa.description: Optional repo-relative or absolute path to the workflow-pack skill folder or SKILL.md file that the AI agent must follow for Jira delivery tasks. Example: .github/skills/add-edit-dotnet-web-api

ticketManager.ai.deliveryAgentWorkflowUr.description: Optional GitLab or web URL for the assigned delivery workflow pack. When set, the Jira start comment includes this link.

ticketManager.ai.deliverySummaryTemplate.description: Optional Jira summary comment template. Supported placeholders: {{summary}}, {{branch}}, {{commitHash}}, {{pushedRef}}, {{artifactNames}}.

ticketManager.ai.deliveryFailureTemplate.description: Optional Jira failure comment template. Supported placeholders: {{failureReason}}, {{branch}}, {{commitHash}}, {{pushedRef}}.
